diffs.diff: illuminance lux (C0DATA, ATIME=0xFF 2.73ms, 1x gain, GA=1: 60/2.73 per count, ignoring IR term): datasheet reading gives 21.98 per count, the part's model has 1, 1
diffs.evidence: Different but equivalent units. The model's sim registers 0xB4 (C0DATA) and 0xB6 (C1DATA) expose raw ADC counts (scale 1, unit 'counts'), exactly what the chip returns; the TSL2572 has no lux register. The lux conversion lives in the driver and matches the datasheet (TAOS132 p.~10, 'Lux Equation'): 'CPL = (ATIME_ms x AGAINx) / (GA x 60); Lux1 = (1 x C0DATA - 1.87 x C1DATA) / CPL; Lux2 = (0.63 x C0DATA - 1 x C1DATA) / CPL; Lux = MAX(Lux1, Lux2, 0)', with 'Integration Time = 2.73 ms x (256 - ATIME)'. Driver: integration_ms() = 2.73*(256-atime), cpl = integration_ms*gain/(ga*60), lux = max(lux1, lux2, 0). At ATIME=0xFF, 1x, GA=1 that gives 1/CPL = 60/2.73 = 21.98 lux per C0 count, identical to the second reading. The example test (ATIME 0xDB, C0=5000, C1=600 -> CPL=101.01/60=1.6835, Lux1=(5000-1122)/1.6835=2303.5) confirms the driver applies it.
